GET /api/waivers/analysis -> waiver-analysis.v1

The §6.2 gate is the whole point of these three. A FAAB number appears ONLY for a league positively determined FAAB; a priority position ONLY for one determined priority; NEITHER when the system is not_determined. The middle artboard is that third case -- the move still renders, the bid does not.

best_move.bid is null when any input is missing, never 0. Claim probability is never returned for any league, so nothing here estimates whether a claim wins. A deadline shows only when availability was confirmed.

GET /api/start-sit/detail -> start-sit-detail.v1   ·   GET /api/moves/:id -> move-detail.v1

Every evidence entry carries its own kind, so a projection is never drawn as a fact. The chip is the mechanism: green Fact = verified, brass Proj = projection, blue Omen = inference, grey Gap = limitation. Same idea on the Ledger receipt, where the categories are league_context / player_game_fact / model_input / omen_inference / limitation.

An unverified scoring format is stated as a limitation and never assumed to be PPR -- the middle artboard. The Ledger receipt shows the other half: a call that pre-dates scoring capture names the PPR fallback as a limitation, and the stored win/loss is translated into measured language, never surfaced raw.

GET /api/league/overview -> league-overview.v1   ·   GET /api/leagues -> league-directory.v1

matchup, standings and activity each carry their own status and FAIL INDEPENDENTLY. A dead matchup read sits beside live standings -- it does not take the screen down. playoff_picture.settings_known is true only for Sleeper today, so ESPN and Yahoo get no cut line rather than a guessed one. The deadline signal is deliberately absent everywhere.

On the switcher: platform groups are ordered by followed-league count, most first, ties alphabetical, and leagues alphabetically within a platform. The server is the single authority on that order -- CLIENTS MUST NOT RE-SORT. is_active is one league; is_followed is many. A per-platform failure degrades that group only, which is the Yahoo row.

POST /api/trade/compare -> trade-compare.v2

Today's native Trade screen is two text fields and a Compare button. The builder here is the rebuild: roster-based, with the two- and three-team shapes as a real control.

The second artboard is the close_needs_context verdict, which is where the contract is most opinionated. Sending league_context AND a bearer token opts into personalized analysis; without it the honest answer is that the two players are close and the roster decides. Unauthenticated returns 200, not 401 -- anyone can read a trade without an account, and the screen has to be complete in that state.

NOT DESIGNED HERE, and deliberately:

· Store listing assets. They come after the app is presentable, per the founder call.
· off_season and no_decision states across all screens.
· player_unavailable on Start/Sit.
· The healthy full League overview -- the existing canvas already carries a matchup + standings screen.
· Trade share output and counters.

All sample data is invented. No real league, team or player figure here was read from a provider.
